To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is no validated PREM available for measuring patient experience in EDs.
there was significant variation in quality of development and performance of four PREMs for EDs, and further validation work is required.
there is no standard measure of patient reported experience for emergency department care and that further development of such a measure is required.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a patient experience questionnaire for emergency department (ED) services.
the development and evaluation of a patient reported experience measure (PREM) for emergency departments (ED) in the UK.
the measurement of patient experience within emergency care service provision and aims to identify patient reported measures (PREMs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence base to support the use of any PREM in ED is weak.
the PREMs currently available are not fit for purpose.
the PREMs currently available for use within emergency departments have uncertain validity, responsiveness and reliability and further validation work is required.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is currently a paucity of validated measures to measure patient experience in emergency care.
PREMs are currently available for use within the ED, however their psychometric properties are uncertain.
the current measures have not been developed rigorously enough to be used to evaluate EDs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PREM field in the ED has been neglected.
there is a need for a standardized PREM for use in the emergency care setting.
the development of PREMs is a complex process that needs to be undertaken with a clear understanding of the purpose of the measure.
